subject: Transportation Systems
title: The Hub-and-Spoke Model
description: A fast breakdown of The Hub-and-Spoke Model for builders.

hook.text: Airlines don't fly everywhere directly. They funnel passengers through hub airports first.

buildup.text: Fly from Boise to Frankfurt? You'll probably connect through Denver or Chicago.

discovery.text: Hubs let airlines fill planes by combining passengers from many small cities onto one big flight.

twist.text: The downside: connections mean delays, missed flights, and lost luggage. Direct routes avoid all that.

climax.text: Low-cost carriers often skip hubs entirely, flying point to point for simpler operations.

punchline.text: Hubs fill big planes. Point-to-point saves time.

quiz.question: Why do airlines use the hub-and-spoke model?
options: To fill large planes by combining passengers from many routes
